summary.headline: IIFL Finance Q4 FY26: consolidated PAT of INR623 crore (up 24% QoQ) and loan AUM of INR1,08,180 crore (up 38% YoY), with gold AUM up 150% YoY to INR52,581 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported consolidated PAT before minority interest of INR623 crore, up 24% QoQ, and pre-provision operating profit of INR1,173 crore, up 80% YoY and 9% QoQ. Loan AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, growing 10% QoQ, with gold the primary growth engine at 62 tonnes of tonnage. Asset quality improved, with GNPA about 1.5% and NNPA 0.7%, while the housing finance arm stayed flat and weak on profitability. Management guided to FY27 AUM growth of 20-25% for gold, 18-20% for housing, a credit cost fall to 1.5-1.7%, and a 100-120 bp cost-of-funds reduction on a rating upgrade. The income tax special audit outcome remained pending, with management expecting orders within days and saying it would appeal any demand.

financial_highlights.metric: Core loan AUM (home, gold, MSME, microfinance)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA down 77 bp YoY, NNPA down 32 bp YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Ind AS provision coverage on NPAs

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR52,581 crore, up 150% YoY and 11% QoQ on 62 tonnes tonnage; management guides 20-25% AUM growth in FY27 if gold prices stay at current levels, and says the new RBI gold rules are fully complied with.

segments.name: Housing finance (IIFL Home Finance)
segments.commentary: AUM was flat QoQ with subdued profitability, partly due to stress in the legacy micro-LAP book (since exited); FY27 guidance is 18-20% AUM/book growth and 25-27% disbursement growth, with yield at about 12%+ on new affordable business versus about 10.55% blended.

segments.name: Microfinance (Samasta)
segments.commentary: Collection efficiency is recovering and asset quality is stabilising; management is growing cautiously, targeting about 20% growth with average microfinance ticket of about INR68,000 and micro-LAP ticket of about INR4.8 lakh, and aims to return to AUM levels of March 2024.

segments.name: Off-book (DA and co-lending)
segments.commentary: Off-book share is 34-36% of AUM, with a target of 40-45%; co-lending book is INR14,384 crore, targeted to grow about 20%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated AUM growth of about 20-25% if gold prices stay at current levels (gold business guided at 20-25%).
FY27 credit cost guided at about 1.5-1.7%, down 120-130 bp from the FY26 guidance of 2.7-3%; management expects ROA to rise from 2.4% toward 3-3.5%, depending on growth.
Housing finance guided to 18-20% AUM/book growth and 25-27% disbursement growth in FY27, with about 100 new branches planned in phases.
Off-book (DA + co-lending) to rise to 40-45% of AUM from 34-36%; co-lending to grow about 20%.
Comfortable leverage up to about 4.5x; management said capital could be raised through debt periodically and equity when the time is right.
A credit rating upgrade from AA (stable) to AA+ could lower cost of funds by 100-120 bp.
capex_capacity: Gold branch expansion: RBI freed branch expansion; management plans to add branches this year, but 'not aggressively'.
Housing finance: about 315 branches (94 emerging, 221 affordable), with about 100 new branches planned this year in phases.
Leverage: net gearing about 3.8x at consolidated level; management says up to 4.5x is comfortable, with the regulatory maximum at about 6-7x depending on capital adequacy.
Liquidity: INR28,165 crore raised during the year plus INR7,046 crore via direct assignments; cash and equivalents including committed lines INR6,638 crore.
demand_pricing: Gold: management said loan demand is independent of gold prices, so tonnage can move sequentially even with AUM growth; Q3 tonnage growth was stronger than Q4.

Housing: prime segment exited on margin grounds; focus on affordable and emerging, where management says 7-8 large players operate and about 80 smaller players have small books. Management said PMAY 2 subsidy with a 5-year lock-in should cut borrower attrition.
Housing competition: management cited Bajaj Housing and PNB Housing entering affordable and near-prime ticket sizes of INR15-25 lakh and said IIFL does not see a challenge to growing its book.
Interest rates: management said money-market rates spiked in March and early April on war-related liquidity tightness, and are now normalising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax special audit and the likely impact (rumoured INR300-400 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on speculative reports. The special audit (mainly gold loans) is complete and the assessment order is expected within days or about a week; the company will appeal any demand and does not expect a material adverse outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a demerger of IIFL Home Finance and Samasta?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an option to demerge into three entities (for ADIA's exit from home finance), but this is a Board decision with no timeline and no active process.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 credit cost and ROA expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is guided to 1.5-1.7% (against 2.7-3% in FY26) and ROA to rise from 2.4% toward 3-3.5%. Credit cost applies only to the on-balance-sheet book (about 10-20% of AUM), not to assigned loans.

qa_highlights.question: How will IIFL adapt to new gold-loan rules (cash-flow assessment for loans above INR2.5 lakh) and branch expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Detailed credit assessment is in place for all loans above INR2.5 lakh and the branch model already does cash-flow assessment. Gold AUM growth is guided at 20-25%, with more branches in underserved areas.

qa_highlights.question: What are the leverage and capital plans, and is equity needed for 20%+ growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can grow without equity if co-lending and DA reach 40-45%; it is comfortable with leverage up to 4.5x and will raise debt periodically and equity when the time is right.

qa_highlights.question: Why was housing AUM muted in FY26, and why are home finance ROE and ROA weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the exit of micro-LAP (overlapping with MFI borrowers) and reduced leverage after an equity raise 2-3 years ago. Growth is expected to lift ROE back toward double digits, and LAP is being focused on at about 18% of the mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rating upgrade roadmap and its impact on cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM crossed INR1 lakh crore, GNPA is 1.5%, and profitability is improving; the remaining gap is capital adequacy, which needs more off-book growth or equity. A move to AA+ could cut funding cost by 100-120 bp, but management would not quantify the rating-upgrade impact.

risks_watch: Outcome and quantum of the income tax special audit and assessment orders for IIFL Finance and group entities; management expects appeals.
Gold price sensitivity: 20-25% gold AUM growth is guided only if prices hold at current levels; tonnage growth was flat QoQ.
New RBI gold-loan norms (cash-flow assessment above INR2.5 lakh) and rising competition from new NBFC entrants and branch expansion.
Housing finance returns: ROE and ROA remain weak with low leverage; yield about 10.55% blended, and the planned pivot to LAP and higher-yield affordable must be executed.
Capital adequacy as leverage rises; off-book (DA and co-lending) must reach 40-45% or equity raised; rating upgrade depends on capital, not only on asset quality.
Possible demerger of IIFL Home Finance and Samasta: Board-level, no timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, gold growth and the off-book model, and firm in saying the tax matter will not be material. Evasive on the timing and terms of the demerger, the tax quantum and rating-upgrade impact, which management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: Our gold loan continues to be the standout performer.
Overall, the quality of our loan book has improved materially.
I believe that our cost of funding can go down easily by 100 to 120 basis points once the rating improves.
So the total off-book proportion, which is DA and co-lending put together will be 34%, 36% in that range.

adds.what: About 100 new housing finance branches planned this year in phases (IIFL Home Finance, on top of about 315 branches)

growth.why: FY27 guidance of about 20-25% consolidated AUM growth (gold 20-25%, housing 18-20%, Samasta ~20%) is backed partly by about 100 planned housing branches and off-book/co-lending growth (co-lending ~20%), while gold growth relies on demand and gold prices with only 'not aggressive' branch expansion, so backing is partial.
